products.summary: The Active 10 Pro has the largest battery of any 5G rugged tablet under $400 we found: 30,000 mAh, which the one published review says lasts several days of moderate use. It adds a 400-lumen camping light, an infrared night-vision camera and a Dimensity 7300 chip, and it carries IP68, IP69K and MIL-STD-810H ratings.
products.fit: Campers, overlanders and anyone who wants a tablet that runs for days off-grid, uses the tablet as a backup light, and is on T-Mobile or AT&T. Not for anyone who needs Verizon, a light tablet, or guaranteed OS updates.
caveats: It weighs 2.7 lb, about three times a Samsung Galaxy Tab Active5, and reviewers compare holding it to holding a large power bank.
No US carrier certifies it. Its LTE bands match T-Mobile and AT&T, its 5G bands only partly match them, and owners of Blackview phones report Verizon rejects the devices.

Ships from overseas: free registered airmail takes 7 to 20 business days, DHL costs $40 extra, and import taxes may apply. Variants are listed with an EU plug charger, so US buyers need a plug adapter.
On 2026-11-06 only the orange 256 GB ($375) and black 512 GB ($429) versions were in stock. Blackview's separate US storefront listed it at $489.99 and out of stock.
Blackview's Trustpilot score is 2.2 of 5 with support delays and slow returns the most common complaints, and the promised Android 15 update was not confirmed delivered as of 2026-11-06.

products.summary: The Active 8 Pro is the cheapest big-battery rugged tablet we found from a maker's own store: 22,000 mAh, a Helio G99 chip and IP68/IP69K/MIL-STD-810H ratings for $289. TechRadar scored it 90% and praised the battery; the trade-offs are 2.2 lb of weight and 4G only.
products.fit: Budget buyers who want days of battery and a stylus for maps, manuals or kids' use, and who are on Wi-Fi, T-Mobile or AT&T.
caveats: Owners on GSMArena report it never received an Android version or security update after launch.
4G LTE only, no 5G, and no US carrier certification; Verizon is not supported.
Ships from overseas with free 7 to 20 business-day airmail or $40 DHL, import taxes may apply, and the charger may come with an EU plug.
Reviewers call it very heavy for a 10-inch tablet at 2.2 lb.
